> **What this deck is.** One presentation answering the three Study B
> questions — do the three methods differ in community composition, does the
> ring differ from the two systemic methods in host gene expression, and does
> community type explain the genes better than the method does. The full
> workings live in the workshop documents — `01-qc.html` (QC),
> `02-ring-vs-systemic.html` and `03-three-arms-review.html` (Question 2),
> `05-q1-three-arms-composition.html` (Question 1) and
> `06-q3-community-vs-method.html` (Question 3); this deck recomputes the
> headline numbers from the data so every slide can be traced. Because
> PowerPoint wants small numbers of things, each slide carries only the
> headline figure plus the sample sizes it is based on.

```{r setup}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(DESeq2)
library(microViz)
library(phyloseq)
library(vegan)
library(ggrepel)

source(here("R/count_tables.R"))

d  <- read_counts("group_b")
sp <- d$species          # 220 species  x 93 samples, raw counts
ge <- d$genes            # 14,226 genes x 93 samples, raw counts
md <- d$metadata         # one row per sample

md <- md |>
  mutate(arm_group = if_else(arm == "ring", "ring", "systemic"))

# Community type, same rule as 01-qc and notebook 02:
# Lactobacillus genus >= half of the sample's species reads.
lacto_taxa <- d$taxonomy |> filter(Genus == "Lactobacillus") |> pull(taxon)
lacto_frac <- colSums(sp[lacto_taxa, , drop = FALSE]) / colSums(sp)
md$community <- ifelse(lacto_frac >= 0.5, "lactobacillus", "anaerobe")

n_arm  <- table(md$arm)          # pill 28, injectable 39, ring 26
n_comm <- table(md$community)    # lactobacillus 48, anaerobe 45
```

# Study B in one slide

## Who, what, how many

- **93 participants**, one vaginal swab each, **one visit** — no time course.
- Each person used one of three hormonal contraceptives **they chose
  themselves** (this is not a randomised trial):

| Method | Samples |
|---|---|
| Pill | 28 |
| Injectable | 39 |
| Vaginal ring | 26 |

- Two sequencing tables for the same 93 samples, features in rows:
  **species** (220 species × 93 samples) and **host genes**
  (14,226 genes × 93 samples), plus 15 cytokines.
- Question for the week: **do the methods differ in their effect?**
  We answer it three ways — on the microbiome, on the genes, and by asking
  whether "community type" explains the genes better than the method does.

## Before any result: what the arms might differ in *besides* the method

**No randomisation. People chose their method.** So any difference between
arms could be the method, or something else that tracks the choice.

We checked the baseline variables (`01-qc.html`):

| Baseline variable | Different across arms? |
|---|---|
| Bacterial vaginosis | no (Fisher p = 0.63) |
| Any STI | no |
| Nugent score | no (p = 0.65) |
| Sequencing batch | no — every arm in both batches |
| **Vaginal pH** | **yes (Kruskal–Wallis p = 0.02)** |

- **The one real imbalance: vaginal pH.** Median 4.55 in the pill arm vs 5.0
  in ring and injectable; the ring arm has no sample below pH 4.4.
- pH tracks both hormones and the vaginal microbiome, so it may be a
  *confounder* (distorting a method comparison) or on the *causal path*
  (part of the method's effect). We show the unadjusted answer and note
  where pH changes it (Question 3 of `03-three-arms-review.html`).
- Everything we present is an **association in a self-chosen comparison**,
  not a trial effect.

## Power: who is compared with whom

Every comparison in this deck, with the samples it is built on:

| Comparison | n | Note |
|---|---|---|
| All three arms | 93 | 28 pill / 39 injectable / 26 ring |
| ring vs pooled systemic | 26 vs 67 | the pooled control is **58 % injectable** |
| ring vs pill | 26 vs 28 | most even ring comparison |
| ring vs injectable | 26 vs 39 | most powerful ring comparison |
| pill vs injectable | 28 vs 39 | the pooling check |
| community type (2 groups) | 93 | 48 lactobacillus / 45 anaerobe |

- The ring arm is the smallest, so **ring comparisons have the least power**;
  a bigger arm finds more "significant" genes for the same true effect.
- With 26–39 per group, only **large gene-expression differences** reach
  FDR < 0.05; small shifts land in the "suggestive" pile.

# Question 1 — do the three methods differ in community composition?

## Q1: the microbiome map, three arms (n = 93)

```{r q1-ordination}
#| label: q1-ordination
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 4.4
#| fig-cap: "Species-table PCoA (CLR + Euclidean) coloured by arm."
ps_sp <- as_counts(dataset = "group_b", table = "microbiome", data = d)
sd <- as(sample_data(ps_sp), "data.frame")
sd$arm <- md$arm[match(sd$sample_id, md$sample_id)]
sample_data(ps_sp) <- sample_data(sd)

ord_sp <- ps_sp |>
  tax_transform("clr", zero_replace = "halfmin") |>
  dist_calc("euclidean") |>
  ord_calc("PCoA")

eig <- attr(ord_sp, "ord")$CA$eig
sh  <- round(100 * eig / sum(eig), 1)

ord_plot(ord_sp, axes = 1:2, color = "arm") +
  stat_ellipse(aes(colour = arm), type = "norm", linewidth = 0.4) +
  labs(x = sprintf("Axis 1 (%s%% of variation)", sh[1]),
       y = sprintf("Axis 2 (%s%%)", sh[2]), colour = "Arm")
```

```{r q1-permanova}
#| label: q1-permanova
dm_sp <- attr(ord_sp, "dist")
meta_sp <- data.frame(sample_data(ps_sp))[rownames(as.matrix(dm_sp)), ]
meta_sp$arm <- factor(meta_sp$arm, levels = c("ring", "pill", "injectable"))
set.seed(1)
# Same model as 05-q1-three-arms-composition.html: batch in, margin test.
q1_main <- adonis2(dm_sp ~ arm + rnaseq_batch, data = meta_sp,
                   permutations = 9999, by = "margin")
q1_r2 <- round(100 * q1_main$R2[1], 1)
q1_p  <- round(q1_main$`Pr(>F)`[1], 3)

pair_sp <- function(a, b) {
  keep <- meta_sp$arm %in% c(a, b)
  out  <- adonis2(as.dist(as.matrix(dm_sp)[keep, keep]) ~ arm,
                  data = droplevels(meta_sp[keep, ]), permutations = 9999)
  tibble(comparison = paste(a, "vs", b),
         n = sum(keep),
         `share of variation (%)` = round(100 * out$R2[1], 1),
         `p (raw)` = out$`Pr(>F)`[1])
}
q1_pairs <- bind_rows(pair_sp("ring", "pill"),
                      pair_sp("ring", "injectable"),
                      pair_sp("pill", "injectable")) |>
  mutate(`p (adjusted, BH)` = p.adjust(`p (raw)`, "BH"))

knitr::kable(
  tibble(comparison = "all three arms", n = nrow(md),
         `share of variation (%)` = round(100 * q1_main$R2[1], 1),
         `p (raw)` = q1_main$`Pr(>F)`[1]),
  caption = "PERMANOVA on species (CLR + Euclidean, adjusted for batch, 9,999 permutations)"
)
```

## Q1: the three methods do **not** carve the microbiome into three

```{r q1-pairs}
#| label: q1-pairs
knitr::kable(q1_pairs,
  caption = "Pairwise PERMANOVA on species (9,999 permutations)")
```

- **Answer: no clear three-way difference.** The main test puts
  `r q1_r2` % of the species-level variation on the method (p = `r q1_p`,
  93 samples) — not significant.
- No pairwise comparison survives adjustment either. If the ring really
  reshaped the community differently from the systemic methods, we cannot
  see it here at this sample size.
- What *does* structure this map is **community type**
  (lactobacillus vs anaerobe, axis 1 holds 36 % — `01-qc.html`). That is the
  split Question 3 follows up.
- No individual species stands out either: **DESeq2 on raw species counts**
  gives hit counts at chance level in every comparison
  (`05-q1-three-arms-composition.html`).
- **Sanity check:** rerun `q1-permanova` with a different `set.seed` — the
  R² stays the same and the p-value should stay near `r q1_p`.

# Question 2 — the ring is local, the others are systemic: do the genes differ?

## Q2: first ordinate the genes, all three arms (n = 93)

```{r q2-ordination}
#| label: q2-ordination
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 4.4
#| fig-cap: "Gene-table PCoA (CLR + Euclidean, genes filtered at >=10 reads in >=10 samples) coloured by arm."
ps_genes <- as_counts(dataset = "group_b", table = "rnaseq",
                      min_count = 10, min_samples = 10, data = d)
sdg <- as(sample_data(ps_genes), "data.frame")
idx <- match(sdg$sample_id, md$sample_id)
sdg$arm       <- md$arm[idx]
sdg$arm_group <- md$arm_group[idx]
sdg$community <- md$community[idx]
sample_data(ps_genes) <- sample_data(sdg)

ord_g <- ps_genes |>
  tax_transform("clr", zero_replace = "halfmin") |>
  dist_calc("euclidean") |>
  ord_calc("PCoA")

eig_g <- attr(ord_g, "ord")$CA$eig
sh_g  <- round(100 * eig_g / sum(eig_g), 1)

ord_plot(ord_g, axes = 1:2, color = "arm") +
  stat_ellipse(aes(colour = arm), type = "norm", linewidth = 0.4) +
  labs(x = sprintf("Axis 1 (%s%% of variation)", sh_g[1]),
       y = sprintf("Axis 2 (%s%%)", sh_g[2]), colour = "Arm")
```

```{r q2-permanova}
#| label: q2-permanova
dm_g <- attr(ord_g, "dist")
meta_g <- data.frame(sample_data(ps_genes))[rownames(as.matrix(dm_g)), ]
meta_g$arm       <- factor(meta_g$arm,       levels = c("ring", "pill", "injectable"))
meta_g$arm_group <- factor(meta_g$arm_group, levels = c("systemic", "ring"))
set.seed(1)
q2_three <- adonis2(dm_g ~ arm + rnaseq_batch, data = meta_g,
                    permutations = 9999, by = "margin")
q2_pooled <- adonis2(dm_g ~ arm_group, data = meta_g, permutations = 9999)
disp_g <- permutest(betadisper(dm_g, meta_g$arm), permutations = 9999)
q2_arm_r2   <- round(100 * q2_three$R2[1], 1)   # row 1 = arm (margin test)
q2_arm_p    <- round(q2_three$`Pr(>F)`[1], 3)
q2_pool_r2  <- round(100 * q2_pooled$R2[1], 1)
q2_pool_p   <- round(q2_pooled$`Pr(>F)`[1], 3)
q2_disp_p   <- round(disp_g$tab$`Pr(>F)`[1], 2)
```

The arms overlap heavily on the map. The formal tests (9,999 permutations,
93 samples):

| Test | Share of variation | p |
|---|---|---|
| arm (adjusted for batch) | `r q2_arm_r2` % | `r q2_arm_p` |
| ring vs pooled systemic | `r q2_pool_r2` % | `r q2_pool_p` |
| spread check (betadisper) | — | `r q2_disp_p` |

- The pooled test's p sits **on the 0.05 line** (reruns with other seeds gave
  0.03–0.055) — call it *suggestive*, not established.
- The spread check says one arm is not just more scattered, which would fake
  a PERMANOVA difference.

## Q2: DESeq2 — ring vs pooled systemic (n = 26 vs 67)

```{r q2-deseq2}
#| label: q2-deseq2
genes_f <- ge[rowSums(ge >= 10) >= 10, ]   # raw counts into DESeq2, always
rownames(md) <- md$sample_id

dds <- DESeq(DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(genes_f, md, design = ~ rnaseq_batch + arm_group),
             quiet = TRUE)
res <- results(dds, contrast = c("arm_group", "ring", "systemic"))
res_df <- as.data.frame(res) |>
  rownames_to_column("ensembl_gene_id") |>
  left_join(d$gene_info |> select(ensembl_gene_id, symbol),
            by = "ensembl_gene_id") |>
  mutate(symbol = coalesce(symbol, ensembl_gene_id),
         padj   = replace_na(padj, 1))
sig <- res_df |> filter(padj < 0.05)
```

- **`r nrow(sig)` genes at FDR < 0.05** (`r sum(sig$log2FoldChange > 0)` up
  in ring, `r sum(sig$log2FoldChange < 0)` down) out of `r nrow(res_df)`
  tested. Smallest FDR `r format(min(sig$padj), digits = 2)`.
- Dropping the blood-contaminated sample `B093` leaves
  **152 of 165 hits standing (92 %)** — the list does not hinge on one
  sample (`02-ring-vs-systemic.html`).
- Caveat from `03-three-arms-review.html`: the raw-p hit lists are about
  twice what chance alone gives, and several top hits are keratins and mucus
  genes — the signal may partly be **cell mix** (how much surface tissue each
  swab caught), not the ring.

```{r q2-volcano}
#| label: q2-volcano
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 4.6
#| fig-cap: "Volcano plot, ring vs systemic. Red: FDR < 0.05; labels: 10 smallest FDR."
res_df |>
  mutate(hit  = padj < 0.05,
         label = if_else(rank(padj) <= 10, symbol, NA_character_)) |>
  ggplot(aes(log2FoldChange, -log10(padj), colour = hit)) +
  geom_point(size = 1, alpha = 0.6, show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("grey70", "firebrick")) +
  geom_text_repel(aes(label = label), size = 2.8, max.overlaps = 20,
                  show.legend = FALSE) +
  labs(x = "log2 fold change (ring vs systemic)",
       y = "-log10 adjusted p-value")
```

## Is pooling pill + injectable fair? (n = 28 vs 39)

```{r pooling-table}
#| label: pooling-table
knitr::kable(
  tribble(
    ~evidence, ~result,
    "pill vs injectable, DESeq2 genes at FDR < 0.05", "11 (chance would give ~5–7)",
    "pill vs injectable, raw p < 0.05", "738 vs ~711 expected by chance",
    "pill vs injectable, PERMANOVA (genes)", "1.4 %, p = 0.54",
    "ring LFC vs pill vs ring LFC vs injectable (all genes)", "r = 0.71, same direction",
  ),
  caption = "Evidence that the two systemic methods behave alike (from 03-three-arms-review.html)"
)
```

- **Why it is fair:** the two systemic arms are near-indistinguishable in the
  genes — 11 hits where chance predicts about 7, PERMANOVA p = 0.54, and the
  ring's log2 fold changes point the **same way against both** (r = 0.71).
- **Two caveats:** the pooled control is 58 % injectable, so "systemic"
  leans that way; and adjusting for the pH imbalance changes the ring-vs-pill
  list from 97 to 191 genes, so the pooled contrast is not the only defensible
  reading.
- Alternative we did not choose: keep the three arms separate
  (`03-three-arms-review.html` does exactly that as a check).

## Q2 verdict

- The gene *profile* differs only subtly between ring and the systemic
  methods: PERMANOVA 1.7 % (p ≈ 0.04, borderline), three-arm test p = 0.10.
- DESeq2 finds **165 genes at FDR < 0.05 (n = 26 vs 67)** — mostly small
  shifts, possibly partly cell-mix rather than a true ring effect.
- The effect, if real, is **modest** — no dramatic reprogramming of vaginal
  tissue. Follow-up: cytokines, cell-mix markers, and an independent cohort
  before calling it.

# Question 3 — group by community type, then test the genes

## Q3: two community types, one map (n = 93)

```{r q3-ordination}
#| label: q3-ordination
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 4.4
#| fig-cap: "Gene-table PCoA (same distances as Q2) coloured by community type."
ord_plot(ord_g, axes = 1:2, color = "community") +
  stat_ellipse(aes(colour = community), type = "norm", linewidth = 0.4) +
  labs(x = sprintf("Axis 1 (%s%% of variation)", sh_g[1]),
       y = sprintf("Axis 2 (%s%%)", sh_g[2]), colour = "Community")
```

```{r q3-permanova}
#| label: q3-permanova
set.seed(1)
q3 <- adonis2(dm_g ~ community + arm_group, data = meta_g,
              permutations = 9999, by = "margin")
q3_comm_r2 <- round(100 * q3$R2[1], 1)   # row 1 = community (margin test)
q3_comm_p  <- round(q3$`Pr(>F)`[1], 4)
```

Community type was assigned from the **species** table (Lactobacillus
≥ 50 % of species reads) and is tested on the **gene** table — the group is
never defined from the table it is tested on.

## Q3: does community type explain the genes better than the method?

```{r q3-margin-table}
#| label: q3-margin-table
knitr::kable(
  tibble(term = c("community type", "method (ring vs systemic)"),
         n = c(93, 93),
         `share of variation (%)` = round(100 * q3$R2[1:2], 1),
         p = round(q3$`Pr(>F)`[1:2], 4)),
  caption = "PERMANOVA on genes: community vs method, each adjusted for the other (9,999 permutations)"
)
```

```{r q3-deseq2}
#| label: q3-deseq2
dds_c <- DESeq(DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(genes_f, md, design = ~ rnaseq_batch + community),
               quiet = TRUE)
res_c <- results(dds_c, contrast = c("community", "anaerobe", "lactobacillus"))
sig_c <- sum(res_c$padj < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE)
```

```{r q3-verdict-table}
#| label: q3-verdict-table
knitr::kable(
  tribble(
    ~grouping, ~`PERMANOVA share (%)`, ~p, ~`DESeq2 genes at FDR < 0.05`,
    "community type (48 vs 45)",  q3_comm_r2, q3_comm_p, sig_c,
    "method, ring vs systemic (26 vs 67)",
      q2_pool_r2, q2_pool_p, nrow(sig),
  ),
  caption = "The two groupings head to head on the same gene table"
)
```

- **Answer: about a tie on the overall map, community ahead gene by gene.**
  On total variation the two groupings explain about the same small share
  (`r q3_comm_r2` % vs `r q2_pool_r2` %), and neither marginal p-value is
  convincing. But gene by gene community type is the stronger signal:
  **`r sig_c` genes at FDR < 0.05** vs 165 for ring vs systemic.
- The two groupings are **not the same thing in disguise**: community
  composition is balanced across the arms (chi-squared p = 0.50), so this is
  a fair head-to-head, not a confounded one.
- Why the mismatch between one map and many genes? A modest, consistent
  shift spread over many genes can pass the per-gene FDR while moving the
  overall profile only slightly.
- Practical upshot for the group project: **adjust for community type** (or
  stratify by it) before interpreting gene differences between methods —
  and expect the method signal, if real, to be the smaller of the two.
- One more reason to adjust: **vaginal pH tracks community type far more
  strongly than it tracks the method** (p ≈ 1e-07 vs 0.02,
  `06-q3-community-vs-method.html`), and the two gene lists barely overlap
  (27 shared genes) — they are different signals, not one signal seen twice.
- Full workings: `06-q3-community-vs-method.html`.

# Wrapping up

## The three answers in three lines

1. **Community composition:** the three methods do **not** differ detectably
   (PERMANOVA `r q1_r2` %, p = `r q1_p`, n = 93). The strong structure is
   community type, not method.
2. **Ring vs systemic genes:** a **small, suggestive** difference — 1.7 % of
   variation (p = `r q2_pool_p`) and 165 genes at FDR < 0.05 (n = 26 vs 67), with
   cell-mix and pH caveats. Pooling the pill with the injectable is
   supported by the data (11 hits, p = 0.54, r = 0.71).
3. **Community type vs method:** about a tie on the overall gene map
   (`r q3_comm_r2` % vs `r q2_pool_r2` % of variation, both weak p-values),
   but community type finds many more individual genes
   (`r sig_c` vs 165). The groupings are independent (community is balanced
   across arms, p = 0.50) — report both, and adjust for community when
   reading method effects.

**Standing caveat for all three:** people chose their method, the arms
differ in vaginal pH, and the ring arm is the smallest (n = 26) — treat every
p-value here as a lead, not a verdict.

## Choices made

- **Answered the workshop's three questions in this order** — composition,
  ring-vs-systemic, community-vs-method — one headline figure each; the
  alternative was to show every plot from the five analysis documents, which
  would bury the answers.
- **Community type defined from the species table and tested on the gene
  table** (Lactobacillus ≥ 50 % of species reads, the notebook 02 rule); a
  stricter cut-off (60 %) or a third intermediate group is the alternative.
- **Species ordination/PERMANOVA on the unfiltered species table** with
  CLR + Euclidean (half-min replacement), matching `01-qc.html`; filtering
  rare species first is the alternative.
- **Gene ordination and DESeq2 on genes with ≥ 10 reads in ≥ 10 samples**,
  matching `02-ring-vs-systemic.qmd`; a stricter filter loses power, a laxer
  one wastes tests.
- **Raw counts into DESeq2** (it normalises itself); CPM or logged values
  would be wrong.
- **Reported both the three-arm and the pooled ring-vs-systemic PERMANOVA**
  — the pooled one is the workshop's question but sits on the p = 0.05 line;
  showing only it would overstate the evidence.
- **Quoted the pairwise DESeq2 and pH-sensitivity numbers from
  `03-three-arms-review.html` rather than recomputing them** here; rerunning
  every fit in the deck is the alternative.
- **Kept the deck as a summary layer over the five analysis documents**
  (`01` QC, `02`+`03` Question 2, `05` Question 1, `06` Question 3) rather
  than re-deriving every sensitivity check on a slide.
- **Used 9,999 permutations and `by = "margin"`** for all PERMANOVA in this
  deck, following the review document's correction of the sequential test.
- **Did not adjust the main results for pH** (it may be on the causal path);
  where pH matters we say so explicitly — the fully adjusted model is the
  alternative.
